results.text: Impact of baseline characteristics and beta-cell function on the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous once-weekly semaglutide: A patient-level, pooled analysis of the SUSTAIN 1-5 trials. To evaluate the impact of relevant patient-level characteristics on the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous, once-weekly semaglutide in subjects with type 2 diabetes.

Efficacy and Safety of Once-Weekly Semaglutide Versus Exenatide ER in Subjects With Type 2 Diabetes (SUSTAIN 3): A 56-Week, Open-Label, Randomized Clinical Trial. To compare the efficacy and safety of once-weekly semaglutide 1.0 mg s.c. with exenatide extended release (ER) 2.0 mg s.c. in subjects with type 2 diabetes.

Semaglutide 2.4 mg in French people living with Class 3 obesity and comorbidities: Baseline characteristics and real-world safety data. - To describe baseline characteristics and safety data of real-world use of semaglutide 2.4 mg. - Patients with a body mass index (BMI) ≥40 kg/m - Overall, 5,797 (62.8%) treatment requests were sent by sites specialized in obesity management. In total, 478 and 8,568 patients were treated within TUA and EAP cohorts respectively, with mean follow-up durations of 1.2 and 4.5 m
